analyst_view.overall: Castellón (2nd, 30 points, unbeaten at home, only 5 goals conceded in 13 games) can go top with a win over Eldense (16th), who ended a three-game losing run by beating Sabadell. Castellón's top scorer Israel Suero (6 of their 24 goals) is out after getting hurt in training before the Valladolid game, which two outlets report and the numbers don't count; Fran Castillo and Rodrigo Rêgo are also injured besides Brignani, while Matías Orozco is back from Colombia duty. Eldense lose captain Jesús Clemente (dislocated shoulder, several weeks) and Fidel Chaves (muscle problem), neither counted by the numbers; Javi Calleja plans to press man-to-man and contest possession. It is a regional derby with a tribute to Jesús de Miguel, and referee Pablo Morales Moreno is slightly below average on cards.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 2.0 of them for Castellón. I lean lower to about 2.6 because Israel Suero, scorer of a quarter of Castellón's league goals, is injured and the numbers don't know it; Eldense are also without Fidel Chaves, and Castellón's defence has conceded only 5 in 13.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and already trim Eldense for 19 corners in their last six. Castellón's possession game should still pin Eldense back without Suero, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards: they add a lot for Eldense's recent cards (20 in six) and take a little off for referee Pablo Morales Moreno (4.6 a game in 7 games). I lean slightly higher to about 5.5 because it is billed as a regional derby, which the numbers do not flag, and Calleja wants man-to-man pressing all over the pitch, which tends to bring fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.5 shots and already trim Castellón for a quieter recent spell. Without Suero Castellón lose their most dangerous finisher and Eldense will try to slow the game by contesting the ball, so I trim it slightly to about 23.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Suero's absence matters most here, since he is the player who turns Castellón's possession into efforts on goal, so I lower it to about 8.3.
